elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term") rather than by mutual written agreement, so the conditional automatic-renewal elements must all be satisfied; they are not (no 30-day opt-out, no 60-day Vendor reminder, no 12-month cap on the renewal term).

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Renewal is for "an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment" — the duration is unbounded and tied to whatever the prior Attachment term was; the redline does not fix the renewal term at 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Operative text requires notice "at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term"; 60 days exceeds the preferred 30-day opt-out.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered language; the margin comment merely notes the preferred position without inserting it.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the renewal clause carries the prior term forward on existing terms and contains no renewal uplift mechanic, so no renewal price increase is permitted by this clause to cap.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered §3.2 now reads "unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — a 60-day window, at the fallback ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a pattern-matching artefact; the spelled-and-numeral form "sixty (60) days" is present in substance.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewal is "for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term" with no uplift language; the separate §13.1 unilateral price-change right (after 12 months, 90 days' notice, fee-free exit) is a change-of-terms mechanic outside the renewal clause and is not a renewal uplift.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the notice window is cut from ninety (90) to sixty (60) days, and the price-cap element is not engaged because the renewal clause carries the prior term forward without any uplift mechanic.
Preferred is not reached: no 30-day opt-out, no 60-day Vendor reminder obligation, and the renewal term is still "equal in duration to the previous term" rather than capped at 12 months.

Minimality fails on the appended declaratory sentence "Customer's non-renewal notice window under this Section 3.2 is no more than 60 days." It duplicates the operative change already achieved by replacing ninety (90) with sixty (60) and adds no independent effect; delete it. It also introduces a one-sided "Customer's" characterisation of a window that the retained sentence makes mutual, creating a needless asymmetry in the drafting.

Intent is preserved: the mutual either-party notice right, the Service Option Attachment structure, the term-duration mechanic and all cross-references survive; no term is left undefined and no retained sentence contradicts the edit.

To repair: strike the added second sentence and rely solely on the sixty (60) day substitution. If escalating to preferred, add (i) "Customer may elect not to renew on thirty (30) days' written notice", (ii) "Vendor will notify Customer at least sixty (60) days before each renewal date", and (iii) "each renewal term will be twelve (12) months".
